failure_summary: All 3/3 runs mis-bind the required zone c1r5 (alias you-immediate, role "the single square where YOU can make four next move", truthBoard afterPlayed, board-verified as X gravity-top <X> at col1 row5) to the OPPONENT, because the render hands the model the same cell twice with opposite owners (opponentPunishment.entryCell="c1r5" and tie.sharedCells=["c1r5"] in the internal-evidence JSON) while the afterPlayed tactics list also carries a board-false entry "double at c1r5 (you, window c1r5-c2r6)" — c2r6 sits two rows above the top of column 2 (ht=3) so the opponent, on move, simply plays c1r5 and wins (solver: afterPlayed col1 = +2 for Gray, all other columns -5); prompt_confusion is a secondary cause for the raw "c2" the model wrote about a column-1 square, and at gpt-5.4-mini (production-fidelity run) that cannot be separated from model capability.
notes: Sub-sampling per rubric: A3, A4, G2, G4, G5 graded on runs 0-1 only; run 2 null for those (not scored, not passed). A5 and A7 graded on all 3 runs. n_runs=3 (this smoke wave has 3 runs, not 5); mechanical keys eval-29|D|0..2 exist and A1/A2/A6/G7a_offered/G7b_offered all pass and were copied verbatim. | A3 run 0: served names c2r6 ("the column 2 finishing square ... that is the line that wins on the spot") as the mechanism; c2r6 is a real X major threat on the decision board but is NOT decisive — the decisive resource is the deep forced win at c2r5 (lostResource.completingCell, pliesToEnd 8), and column 2 lands at c2r4 (prompt Decision block states this verbatim), so no square is "taken" at c2r6 and nothing wins on the spot. | A4 run 0: three board-false claims — (a) "the move that takes [c2r6]" (better move lands c2r4); (b) "wins on the spot" (pliesToEnd 8, c2r6 unreachable, col2 ht=3); (c) the phrase "the column 2 upper square" is wrapped in [zone:c1r5], which lights column 1 row 5. | A4 run 1: "leaves an immediate threat at [zone:c1r5] ... for your opponent" is board-false — visualize_board on 4222425326433430153304516651020 shows "col1 row5 (X) [GT]", i.e. YOUR gravity-top threat; the opponent has no four-completing square on afterPlayed (opponentPunishment.pliesToEnd 9). | A5 run 2: fails A5a on the literal v1 banned-term list — "that is the line that wins on the forced route" uses "route", a render_decision field name explicitly listed. FLAG FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: this is a borderline literal application — "route" appears ZERO times in the assembled prompt (grepped), so the model coined it as ordinary English rather than echoing a field, and a player would not read it as internal jargon. Graded fail to keep the frozen list applied literally; discount if the wave re-scopes A5a. | A7 all 3 runs: A7b. Run 0 — "the column 2 upper square" highlights c1r5; "that is the line" names a line that is never located (you-major-line / opp-key-line offered, unused). Run 1 — "the key square in column 2" is unwrapped and ambiguous between c2r4/c2r5/c2r6, "their own four-in-a-row line" is never located (opp-key-line unused), and the c1r5 referent describes an opponent object that does not exist there. Run 2 — "the column 2 square that makes four right after your move" highlights c1r5 (column 1), and "their central line" is unlocated. A7c is N/A for run 0 and passes for runs 1-2 (column 2 is named as the move that keeps the fork). | G1 all 3 runs: the served answer is unfaithful to the rendered artifact — every run drops at least one REQUIRED handle (run 0 omits you-future-fork; runs 1 and 2 omit you-major), and run 0 additionally asserts "wins on the spot" against the artifacts own frame "deep on a forced line" plus the explicit prompt rule at the Reading key ("never future tense ... when the better move wins outright" / "deep on a forced line ... not a current threat"). | G2 runs 0-1: guardrail "You gave up a win AND handed the opponent their own; name both lines with their horizons" is not honored — run 0 gives a false horizon for your line ("on the spot") and only "later" for the opponents; run 1 gives no horizon and no location for the opponents line at all. | G4 runs 0-1: checked against render_decision.finalMovestring = 422242532643343015330451665102146556600 (= lostResource.finalMovestring, NOT an alternate PV). On that line X wins at c2r5 on ply 39 with c1r5 already occupied by X 39/X 31; run 0s "wins on the spot at c2r6" and run 1s "immediate threat at c1r5 for your opponent" both contradict it. | G5 runs 0-1: the rendered afterPlayed tactics list entry "double at c1r5 (you, window c1r5-c2r6)" is board-false as a fork under the terms own shipped definition ("two winning squares at once — your opponent cannot block both"): c2r6 is not reachable (column 2 height 3) and the opponent to move blocks c1r5 and wins. A render bug to REPORT, and the likely seed of the c1r5 confusion. | G6 passes all runs: patternOnAfterBestBoard is null, case win_to_lose with both a forfeited win and an opponent win — L6 is the correct route. | G3 passes all runs: afterBest is shown:false with reason "tag-set identical to the decision board", verified true (both boards show only "major at c2r6 (you)"); no run needed it. | G7 fails all 3 runs on the JUDGMENT half only (membership G7a/G7b pass, annotationRepairs empty in all runs): every run binds [zone:c1r5] to a phrase whose meaning contradicts the aliass role, and run 1 additionally binds [term:immediate_threat] (description: "a square where four-in-a-row completes on the very next move") to the opponent.

All 3/3 runs resolved the ambiguity the wrong way and told the player the opponent threatens four at c1r5, which the afterPlayed board contradicts (col1 row5 is X, gravity-top).

counterexamples.evidence: c2r6 is genuinely shared — X has the diagonal c5r3,c4r4,c3r5,c2r6 (decision board: Major threats col2 row6 (X)) and Gray wins on row 6 c2r6,c3r6,c4r6,c5r6 (opponentPunishment.finalMovestring, move 40 at c2r6). The offered role names only the YOUR side, so run 0 built the whole answer around c2r6 as your immediate win ("wins on the spot"), which is false: column 2 lands at c2r4 and the real win is c2r5, 8 plies deep.
